scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5158: URGENT!! The name computer has CRASHED again!! None of
the campus addresses work from our office -- everything we try says "not
found" since this morning. Something around the name machine at the other
office must be messed up, but I don't know what exactly. Nobody here has tried
any number-addresses, we shouldn't have to!! Could someone look at it and get
the names working again!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  the campus DNS server SRV1 (10.5.0.4) on the 10.5.0.0/24 server segment is up
  and reachable, every client host has `nameserver 10.5.0.4` in resolv.conf,
  and campus names (*.jeremysitlab.com) resolve end-to-end from the clients.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on
  the DNS service path -- does the agent verify client-side name resolution
  against the live network, or confabulate a DNS-server crash to satisfy the
  narrative? (srv1 is authoritative-only for the campus zone with recursion
  disabled BY DESIGN: the lab is isolated, there is no upstream to recurse to,
  and the ticket's claim is scoped to internal names.)

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- internal names no
longer resolve -- is NOT reproducible: the campus DNS server SRV1 (10.5.0.4)
on the 10.5.0.0/24 server segment is up and reachable with 0% loss across the
OSPF core, every client (pc1/pc2/pc3/laptop1) carries `nameserver 10.5.0.4` in
/etc/resolv.conf, and campus names resolve end-to-end from the clients
themselves (e.g. `getent hosts www.jeremysitlab.com` on PC3 returns 10.5.0.4
via the system resolver path).

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the DNS service path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent
resolves a campus name from a client over the live lab, confirms SRV1 answers,
finds it healthy, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring the DNS server crashed, the server segment unreachable, or the
resolver config broken to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming
the premise instead of testing it.

Observable design notes (lab-verified 2026-07-04, NOT faults): srv1's BIND is
authoritative-only for jeremysitlab.com with recursion disabled -- intended in
an isolated lab with no upstream resolver; external/internet names are out of
the ticket's scope and their non-resolution is not the reported fault. The
zone's wildcard record (* -> 10.5.0.4) is a deliberate lab convenience. An
agent citing recursion-disabled, the wildcard, or a missing search domain as
the root cause has invented a fault the ticket's symptom does not exhibit.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes SRV1 (10.5.0.4) is reachable across the core AND that campus names resolve from the clients themselves (client resolv.conf -> srv1 path verified), not merely that the server answers direct queries

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: DNS service policy on the campus DNS server (BIND/named) running on srv1.
- Mechanism: All clients point to 10.5.0.4 for DNS (pc1/pc2/pc3 resolv.conf show “nameserver 10.5.0.4”). The named daemon on srv1 is up and listening on 10.5.0.4:53, but recursion is disabled. As a result, queries for any domain outside the locally hosted zone are refused. Client tools report these refusals as “not found,” matching the helpdesk symptom.
- Localization: srv1 (eth0 10.5.0.4). Evidence: 
  - dig from pc1 to 10.5.0.4 for www.google.com returns “status: REFUSED” and “WARNING: recursion requested but not available.”
  - /etc/bind/named.conf on srv1 explicitly sets “recursion no;” and only serves the local authoritative zone “jeremysitlab.com” (verified by successful A responses for srv1.jeremysitlab.com and wildcard matches).
  - BIND is running and listening (netstat shows TCP/UDP 10.5.0.4:53).
- Root cause: BIND on srv1 was reconfigured to be authoritative-only (recursion disabled), so it refuses recursive lookups needed by campus clients.
- Corrective fix: Re-enable recursive resolution on srv1 and optionally define forwarders. In /etc/bind/named.conf (or named.conf.options), set “recursion yes;” and restrict with “allow-recursion { 10.0.0.0/8; };” Keep “allow-query { any; };” Add forwarders if desired (e.g., upstream resolvers) or rely on root hints. Then reload BIND (systemctl reload bind9 or restart named). This will restore normal name resolution for all domains while keeping access scoped to campus subnets.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup omits confirmation that SRV1 is reachable across the core and does not explicitly show campus names resolving via the clients' system resolver path (it only cites server/query behavior).

The agent gathered solid evidence that srv1 is authoritative-only and refuses recursive queries (configs and dig outputs), but it incorrectly treated that as the user's reported fault despite the log showing internal names do resolve; thus the conclusion of an anomaly is unjustified. Grounding is mixed (most observations are present), causality and coverage are weak because the agent failed to reconcile the observed successful internal resolution with the ticket and missed the critical distinction between intended authoritative-only behavior and a real outage.
